earlier_scan.note: Extinct Arawakan; attested only by a wordlist in the Natterer nachlass (Ramirez 2020 classification); no phonology/stress description exists.

sources.citation: Meira, Sérgio. 2020. A Study of the Genetic Relation between Mawayana and Wapishana (Arawakan Family). Revista Brasileira de Línguas Indígenas 2(1): 70-104.
sources.note: Cited by Glottolog for Aroaqui subclassification only; open-access journal but site returned 404; unlikely to contain Aroaqui phonology.

sources.citation: Martius, Carl Friedrich Philipp von. 1867. Beiträge zur Ethnographie und Sprachenkunde Amerika's zumal Brasiliens, Bd. 1 (Zur Ethnographie) and Bd. 2 (Wörtersammlung brasilianischer Sprachen / Glossaria linguarum Brasiliensium). Leipzig: Fleischer.
sources.note: Checked in case Natterer's Aroaqui list had been printed here: it was not. Bd. 1 chapter 'Die Aroaquis, Aruac, Arawaaks' (pp. 686-703) and Bd. 2 list 'Aruac, Aruwaac, Aroaqui' (pp. 307-311) both concern the Guianese Arawak (Lokono; Moravian/Surinam material), not the Rio Negro language aroa1234. No stress remark.

sources.citation: Wikipedia (en) 'Aroaqui language' and Wikipedia (pt) 'Língua aroaqui', citing Ramirez 2020 vols. III-IV.
sources.note: Only a ~55-item flora/fauna/artefact vocabulary 'collected by Johann Natterer (1832) in Airão', as normalised by Ramirez 2020. Two items carry an acute accent (maiʃé 'demon', Menétʃu 'Mary') with no explanation; no phonology or stress statement.

sources.citation: Jolkesky, Marcelo Pinho de Valhery. 2016 [corrected 2017]. Estudo arqueo-ecolinguístico das terras tropicais sul-americanas. PhD dissertation, Universidade de Brasília.
sources.note: Silent. 'aroaki †' appears once, as a leaf under WAPIXANA-PARAWANA in the Arawak classification tree; no Aroaqui data, no phonology.

sources.citation: Adelaar, Willem F.H. & Hélène B. Brijnen. 2014. Johann Natterer and the Amazonian languages. Revista Brasileira de Linguística Antropológica 6(2): 333-352.
sources.note: Nothing about Aroaqui stress. Names 'Arauaqui (Aroaqui)' once among Natterer's Rio Negro Arawak lists (p. 337). Pp. 339-340 discuss Natterer's diacritics in general: the acute accent on é marks vowel quality (a central or mid front vowel), 'the motivation behind these different uses of é is not clear'; no accent/stress interpretation offered for any language.

sources.citation: Loukotka, Čestmír. 1968. Classification of South American Indian languages (ed. Johannes Wilbert). Los Angeles: Latin American Center, University of California. p. 135 (Arawak stock, North Central division, 'n. Languages of the Manáo group': entry 'Arauaqui').
sources.note: Nothing: Loukotka records the language as having no data at all ('[Nothing.]'), so there is no vocabulary, phonology or accent remark. Useful only as the classic classification record and as evidence that no pre-1989 source carries Aroaqui data.

sources.citation: Natterer, Johann. 1832 [ms. 1817-1835]. 'Unterhalb Airaó, Rio negro – July 1832 – Nation Aroaqui' (wordlist W50, ms. fol. 226-229), in: Wortlisten von Indianersprachen in Brasilien. Universitätsbibliothek Basel, UBH T 2 (Nachlass J. J. von Tschudi). Digitised on e-manuscripta.ch, scan pp. [689]-[696], DOI 10.7891/e-manuscripta-128842, Public Domain Mark (online since 2022-03-02).
sources.note: No prose about pronunciation at all. The Aroaqui forms (Latin script; German glosses in Kurrent) carry acute accents on many items — e.g. menétʃu 'Gott / nossa senhora', Maiʃé 'Teufel', apá 'Vater', nodáni 'Sohn', nodanítʃehe 'Tochter', noé mutʃchi 'Mann', madítʃcha kavale 'Alter', nodókütʃé 'Grossmutter', medéolí 'Bruder', néenaálí 'Schwester', kaádü 'Sand', kaliá 'See', seidéju 'Nacht' — plus underlined vowels and ü/ö graphs; accent position varies across words and some words carry two accents. These are raw diacritics in a wordlist with no key (Adelaar & Brijnen 2014: 339-340 note Natterer…

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.3, languoid Aroaqui (aroa1234), with reference records 581555, 665291, 143256, 154551, 546819.
sources.note: No descriptive reference. Comment: 'Aroaqui is an extinct Arawakan language attested by a wordlist in the re-discovered Natterer nachlass (Nowotny 1949, Kann 1989, Adelaar & Brijnen 2014). It has been shown by Ramirez 2020: 539-574 to be an independent language of the Negro-Roraima subgroup.' Glottolog's most extensive descriptions: Ramirez 2020 and Adelaar & Brijnen 2014, both 'a wordlist or less'.

sources.citation: Ramirez, Henri. 2020. Enciclopédia das línguas Arawak, vol. IV: Bancos de dados (Anexo II: Listas de vocabulário arawak). Curitiba: Editora CRV. 254 pp.

sources.note: Holds the full normalised Natterer Aroaqui vocabulary (the primary data); would show whether accent marks are carried through the whole list.

sources.citation: Ramirez, Henri. 2020. Enciclopédia das línguas Arawak: acrescida de seis novas línguas e dois bancos de dados, vol. III: Os outros subgrupos Arawak (cap. 1, O subgrupo Central; Aroaqui section = pp. 539-574 of the 2019 preprint per Glottolog). Curitiba: Editora CRV. 290 pp.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: The only modern treatment of the Natterer Aroaqui list; Ramirez normally reconstructs a segment inventory for wordlist-only languages and may comment on how he read Natterer's accent marks (the two acute-accented items maiʃé, Menétʃu reproduced on Wikipedia come from here). Best chance of any accent remark, though a stress rule is unlikely.

sources.note: The sole primary attestation; Natterer's diacritics are the only possible trace of accent placement. No statement of stress will exist, but an edition would let accent marks be tabulated.
